Matthew sets the coming together by what follows: 'Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife' (Matthew 1:24). 'Of the Holy Ghost' uses the same ek ('of') as 1 John 5:1: 'every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.' Those born of God there have fathers in the flesh. HELD. The defender establishes through interlocking texts that Christ was conceived of the Holy Ghost without the procreative act of a human male [L1][L4]. The challenger fails to sustain its alternative reading that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal, as that claim directly contradicts the plain testimony of Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 [L1][L3]. The legal and covenant reckoning through David's house does not overturn the stated miraculous origin [L3][L4].
RESULT: DEFENDER WINS -- The scriptures in the record demonstrate that Christ was conceived of the Holy Ghost without a human biological father.
CLAUSE: HELD-1 -- n=6 w=0 k=0
KEYSTONE: D6 -- STANDS
DEFENSE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- The defender exhibited two or more prior layers for each link and answered every proven witness pressed against it.
CONCEDED LINKS: 0
CHALLENGE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The challenger's first link failed to exhibit its footing against Matthew 1:18 and left that pressed witness unanswered under ruling 412.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 1
Challenger premise 1: UNEXHIBITED (answer to pressed witness Matthew 1:18 fails to meet the meaning pressed, leaving it unanswered under ruling 372 and ruling 412)
COLLISION POINTS
D1: STANDS -- GROUND: Matthew 1:18-20 names the Holy Ghost as the procreative source and names no human progenitor.
D2: STANDS -- GROUND: Matthew 1:16 departs from the active begat formula of Matthew 1:2 to trace the birth through Mary alone.
D3 vs C1 (Matthew 1:18): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- Matthew 1:18 states "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" [L1], where sunerchomai (G4905) means to come together [L2], and Matthew 1:25 confirms Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L3] (Commitment 3) -- GROUND: Matthew 1:18 excludes any coming together prior to the conception found of the Holy Ghost.
FORCED: D3 vs C1 -- MEANS [Defender R3]: "the finding with child came before any coming together -- [L2] synerchomai (G4905, come together) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 \"And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\"" -- ANSWER [Challenger R3]: "The verse dates the finding. Matthew sets the coming together by what follows: 'Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife' (Matthew 1:24). That is the taking of Deuteronomy 20:7, 'hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her.' The order is Matthew's own: espoused, found with child before the taking, then taken. 'Of the Holy Ghost' uses the same ek ('of') as 1 John 5:1: 'every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.' Those born of God there have fathers in the flesh. John 3:6 keeps the two kinds apart: 'That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.' It fits the link: the finding falls inside the espousal, before the taking." -- FAILS: "It fits the link: the finding falls inside the espousal, before the taking."
D4: STANDS -- GROUND: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 define the sign as a virgin conceiving, aligned with Genesis 24:16 and 24:43.
D5: STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's fatherhood as supposition and Luke 2:49 records the Lord's own distinction.
D6: STANDS -- GROUND: Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 show Davidic descent according to the flesh through the woman without biological paternity.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:20 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "the row carrying \"of the Holy Ghost\" names the son of David and his wife in the same breath." -- ANSWER: "Matthew 1:20 itself, 'Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost'. It names Joseph as the one told and the Holy Ghost as the source. It does not name Joseph as the source." -- MEETS -- "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
ANSWER CHECK: 1 John 5:1 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "gennaō with ek and God names a Spirit origin of men who have fathers." -- ANSWER: "1 John 5:1, 'him also that is begotten of him'... speak of persons already living who are 'born of God'. They are a second birth set beside a first, as John 3:6 shows... Matthew 1:20 speaks of 'that which is conceived in her', the child at its first conception, and gives the Holy Ghost as its source." -- MEETS -- "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God"
ANSWER CHECK: John 3:6 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "Spirit origin and flesh origin are two kinds, set side by side." -- ANSWER: "John 3:6 sets two origins side by side, and Matthew 1:20 names the Spirit's." -- MEETS -- "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
ANSWER CHECK: 1 John 3:9 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "being \"of God\" by his seed is said of believers with human fathers." -- ANSWER: "Both speak of persons already living who are 'born of God'. ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:32 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "the covenant son is set on David's throne." -- ANSWER: "These give God as father and David as the remote father. ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:21 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "Joseph is given the father's naming act." -- ANSWER: "Matthew 1:21, 'thou shalt call his name JESUS'... The naming is not the father's act only. ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:62 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "the naming is the father's act." -- ANSWER: "Luke 1:62, 'And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.' ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 11:11 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "\"born of\" a woman is said of a man whose father is named." -- ANSWER: "Matthew 11:11, 'Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist'... I grant these name or imply fathers. They do not make Matthew 1:16 do so, since Matthew 1:16 breaks the 'begat' form that Matthew 1:2 sets." -- MEETS -- "Among them that are born of women"
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:13 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "the naming formula given to Zacharias is the formula given to Joseph." -- ANSWER: "To Zacharias the angel says 'bear thee a son' (Luke 1:13). ANSWER CHECK: Luke 2:48 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "the mother herself names Joseph as father." -- ANSWER: "Luke 2:48, 'behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing'. ANSWER CHECK: Job 14:1 -- [Defender R3] -- MEANS: "\"born of a woman\" marks a man's birth and mortality." -- ANSWER: "Job 14:1, 'Man [that is] born of a woman'... Both sides exhibit lower-layer footing for their principal [L4] inferences; the decisive defects in the challenge are failures to fit or answer particular proven witnesses, not floating inference. RESULT: DEFENDER WINS -- The record more strongly supports conception without a human begetter than the challenger's proposed knowing during the espousal.

KEYSTONE: D6 -- STANDS -- Christ had no biological father remains the conclusion of the defender's surviving, narrowed chain.
DEFENSE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- Each listed premise receives exhibited lower-layer footing and an answer meeting the proven witnesses, including substantive narrowing rather than surrender of its declared link.

CHALLENGE STANDING: COLLAPSED -- L=6 c=5 -- Although its blocks exhibit multiple lower layers, most listed premises retain a proven witness whose meaning their answers fail to meet.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 5 -- Premise 1 is spared. Premise 2: UNEXHIBITED, Matthew 1:25 remains incompatible with the pregnancy-limited abstinence the challenger asserts. Premise 3: UNEXHIBITED, its answers do not fit the conception and virgin-with-child witnesses. Premise 4: UNEXHIBITED, the answer restates intent, character, and fear without addressing the pressed explanation of the publick example. Premise 5: UNEXHIBITED, Luke 2:43 is named without answering the meaning pressed concerning the mistaken supposition. Premise 6: UNEXHIBITED, its answer imports the failed covenant answer to Matthew 1:20. These are answer failures under Commitments 3 and 5, not findings that their blocks lack two lower-layer kinds.
CONTRADICTIONS: NONE FOUND. The defender's removal of 'alone' and 'only' narrows what the respective genealogy and household links independently establish; the close does not restore those words as independent exclusions.   "reasoning": "HELD. Mary was a virgin espoused to Joseph who knew no man [L1][L2], and her conception was of the Holy Ghost before they came together [L1][L2][L3]. Matthew's genealogy terminates the active patrilineal pattern of begetting at Joseph by shifting to the passive birth of Jesus from Mary [L1][L2], while Scripture expressly qualifies Joseph's paternal relation as supposed [L1][L2][L3]. The challenger's counter-construction of an espousal union contradicts the explicit textual timeline of Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 [L1][L4].
RESULT: DEFENDER WINS. The verses of the record, read together line upon line, prove that Christ was conceived of the Holy Ghost without a human biological father.

RULING -- D1 vs C1 (Luke 1:34) -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Mary's present state of knowing no man is answered by the Holy Ghost overshadowing her to bring forth the holy thing without a husband.
NAMED BY: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" (Luke 1:35)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- "I will evaluate whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture read precept upon precept, rather than relying on surface phrasing or literal absences."
APPLIED: the rule requires evaluating whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture; the record shows Mary's question is answered by the Holy Ghost rather than a husband; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D2 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18) -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before coming together with Joseph, excluding any union within the espousal.
NAMED BY: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- "I will evaluate whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture read precept upon precept, rather than relying on surface phrasing or literal absences."
APPLIED: the rule requires evaluating whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture; the record shows the conception occurred before coming together and was of the Holy Ghost; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D3 vs C6 (Matthew 1:16) -- CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN
CLAIM: The genealogical pattern of a father begetting shifts at Jesus to being born of Mary alone, withholding a human begetter.
NAMED BY: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" (Matthew 1:16)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- "I will evaluate whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture read precept upon precept, rather than relying on surface phrasing or literal absences."

NAMED BY: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" (Luke 3:23)
RULE: Commitment 3 -- "I will evaluate whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture read precept upon precept, rather than relying on surface phrasing or literal absences."
APPLIED: the rule requires evaluating whether links agree with the demonstrated meaning of scripture; the record shows Luke specifically frames Jesus' relation to Joseph as supposed; so CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
RULING -- D6 -- STANDS
CLAIM: Christ had no biological father because scripture attributes his conception solely to the Holy Ghost in a virgin woman.
NAMED BY: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20)
RULE: Commitment 8 -- "I will evaluate arguments built layer by layer across text, original languages, and cross-references, breaking a chain only where a link cannot reconcile with scripture or is dismantled by its own side."
APPLIED: the rule requires breaking a chain only where a link cannot reconcile with scripture or is dismantled by its own side; the record shows the defender's chain coheres across all verses without being broken or dismantled; so STANDS.
COLLISION POINTS
D1 vs C1 (Luke 1:34): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (Commitment 3) -- Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L1] with ginōskō (G1097, to know) [L2] and Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L3] shows her non-knowing is answered by the Holy Ghost's overshadowing and not a husband -- GROUND: The angel explicitly provides the Holy Ghost as the source in direct answer to Mary knowing no man.
D2 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (Commitment 3) -- Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L1] with synerchomai (G4905, to come together) [L2] and Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L3] refutes an espousal union -- GROUND: Matthew explicitly places the conception of the Holy Ghost prior to any coming together.
D3 vs C6 (Matthew 1:16): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (Commitment 3) -- Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." [L1] with gennaō (G1080, to beget) [L2] and Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;" [L3] demonstrates that the active verb of begetting is withheld from Joseph -- GROUND: Matthew shifts from active paternal begetting to the passive birth through Mary alone.
D4 vs C5 (Luke 3:23): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (Commitment 3) -- Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli," [L1] with nomizō (G3543, to suppose) [L2] and Luke 2:49: "And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L3] establishes that the paternal relation was a reckoning and not biological paternity -- GROUND: Scripture explicitly qualifies the sonship under Joseph as a supposition.
D5: STANDS -- GROUND: Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15 name the woman as source of the seed and were answered in CR4.
D6: STANDS -- GROUND: The keystone stands as the interlocking chain shows conception of the Holy Ghost without a human father, answered in CR4.

The conception rows name the Holy Ghost as the source of what was begotten in Mary: [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" with the margin "conceived: Gr. begotten," [L2] gennaō (to beget), and [L3] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." Read with [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost," those verses agree with no man's begetting at that conception. The step from David's loins to Joseph as the begetter cannot take that meaning, and Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's sonship "as was supposed."
CONTRADICTION -- DEFENDER -- EARLIER ([CR3], "I drop the claim that the span of heōs in Matthew 1:25 reaches back to the conception.") -- LATER ([CR4], "So the verse fits a conception without a man's knowing.") The close sentence is disregarded; D2 is graded on the [CR3] narrowing.
RESULT: DEFENDER WINS -- The verses that speak of the conception name the Holy Ghost and place the child before Joseph and Mary came together, and the verses that call Joseph father do not state that he begat the child.
CLAUSE: HELD-1 -- n=6 w=0 k=0
KEYSTONE: D6 -- STANDS -- the last declared link, that Christ had no biological father and that Joseph was not the begetter, stands: no declared link is withdrawn, and no defender link is graded broken.
DEFENSE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- Each premise listed against the defender was kept, or narrowed without keeping a dropped limb, on two prior layers, and each proven witness under those premises was engaged in [CR3] or [CR4].
CONCEDED LINKS: 0 -- none counted. Premises 1 through 6 are spared: 1 exhibited Matthew 1:20, gennaō (to beget), Matthew 1:18 and Luke 1:35; 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 were narrowed and the kept words still have two prior layers, and the proven presses were met.
CHALLENGE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=2 -- Two of the six premises listed against the challenger left a proven witness unanswered; that is not most of the list, so the challenge is not collapsed, and it is not self-supported.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 2 -- premise 1 UNEXHIBITED (Luke 3:23 answer FAILS: the cut gloss does not carry "supposed"); premise 2 UNEXHIBITED (Matthew 1:21 MISSES: the answer does not engage "bring forth" against "bear thee"). Premises 3, 4, 5 and 6 are spared: each [DR3] block exhibits two prior layers and meets its proven presses.

{

  "reasoning": "SUPERSEDED BY CURE: verdict BROKEN to HELD; see the cure lines below
BROKEN. [L1][L3] The defender exhibited a connected case rather than isolated assertions, but did not answer the meaning pressed through Hebrews 7:10 with Matthew 1:2 against D6. [L4] This is a failure to meet a listed, proven witness, not a judgment that an inference must appear verbatim in one verse. The other disputed readings remain footed but do not independently settle the question.
RESULT: UNDERDETERMINED -- recomputed after the cure from the cured lines (RETRACTED D6 vs C1 (DEFENDER LINK BROKEN to UNDERDETERMINED)): HELD-1, CHALLENGE STANDING SELF-SUPPORTED, no collision line stands graded CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN.
CLAUSE: HELD-1  -- n=6 w=0 k=0
KEYSTONE: D6 -- BROKEN -- The conclusion that Christ had no biological father remains asserted, but its answer to the each-link descent argument is an absence argument rather than a demonstrated fit.
DEFENSE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- All six link-round blocks exhibit at least two prior layer kinds, but premise 6 is UNEXHIBITED through an unanswered proven witness; the other five premises are spared.
CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 6: UNEXHIBITED (a pressed witness left unanswered), specifically Hebrews 7:10's each-link meaning; premises 1–5 are supported in their retained, narrowed forms. None is VOID, and dropping subsidiary grounds in premises 2–4 and 6 does not surrender their retained links.
CHALLENGE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- All six listed challenger claims exhibit prior-layer footing and engage their proven witnesses; their inferences are evidence even where they do not compel the defender's agreement.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 0 -- Premises 1–6 are spared: each has quoted verse footing, supporting verses or counted source-language footing, and an answer meeting the meaning pressed; none is VOID or expressly surrendered.
PREMISE QUOTE CHECK: Against the defender, premise quotes 1–5 occur in CR1 or CR2, and premise 6 occurs in CR2; against the challenger, all six premise quotes occur in DR2. The charges paraphrase those claims without adding a stronger negation or universal. The ASSUMES formulations are checked against the retained arguments, not voided for their wording.
FLOATING INFERENCES: NONE in the operative link-round blocks. Each defender and challenger block exhibits [L1] with [L2] or [L3], usually both; unfavorable answers and disputed meanings do not by themselves make an inference floating.
CONTRADICTION -- DEFENDER -- EARLIER (CR3, "I drop the claim that the span of *heōs* in Matthew 1:25 reaches back to the conception.") -- LATER (CR4, "Whatever the span, the text states Joseph did not know her through the pregnancy and up to the birth.")
CONTRADICTION -- DEFENDER -- EARLIER (CR3, "I drop the claim that the span of *heōs* in Matthew 1:25 reaches back to the conception.") -- LATER (CR4, "So the verse fits a conception without a man's knowing.")
WITHDRAWAL CHECK: The Matthew 1:25 conception-span limb is REASSERTED IN CR4 "Whatever the span, the text states Joseph did not know her through the pregnancy and up to the birth." The specifically flagged sentence, "So the verse fits a conception without a man's knowing.", is disregarded. D2 STANDS WITHOUT IT because its retained CR3 argument combines Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:31 and Luke 1:34; this is a narrowed argument, not withdrawal of D2.
WITHDRAWAL CHECK: The general assertion that Isaiah's sign excludes approach STANDS WITHOUT IT because CR3 retains Matthew's application of Isaiah 7:14 to the conception described in Matthew 1:18; the concession allows children conceived by approach to be signs.
WITHDRAWAL CHECK: The naming limb STANDS WITHOUT IT because CR3 retains Matthew 1:16 and Luke 3:23, and CR4 expressly explains why naming does not prove begetting.
WITHDRAWAL CHECK: The assumption concerning Mary's house STANDS WITHOUT IT as an assumption removed from the retained CR3 formulation; premise 6 is counted instead for its unanswered witness, not for demanding a row that states an inferred conclusion.
COLLISION POINTS:
D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 and CR4 distinguish the source of this conception from Joseph's marital status, while DR3 places conception within the espousal; GROUND: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" and "Mary thy wife" are accommodated through different, exhibited readings.
D1 vs C4 (Matthew 1:20; John 3:6): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 answers the believer parallels by distinguishing this conception, while DR3 preserves spiritual origin beside fleshly descent; GROUND: Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" and John 3:6 "that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" leave the competing applications disputed after the answers.
D2 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18; Luke 1:34): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 answers the timing witnesses with its narrowed announcement-to-finding argument, and DR3 answers with the distinction between espousal and taking; GROUND: Matthew 1:18 "before they came together" and Luke 1:34 "I know not a man" support the defender's reading without conclusively defeating the challenger's exhibited household-timing reading.
D3: STANDS -- CR3 answers Isaiah 8:3 and Isaiah 8:18 by allowing approach-born children to be signs while retaining Matthew's fulfilment application, and answers Genesis 24:16 and Exodus 2:8 through their respective contexts; GROUND: the retained link is the virgin prophecy and its declared fulfilment, not the surrendered claim that every sign excludes approach.
D4 vs C1 (Matthew 1:16; Luke 3:23): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 and CR4 answer pedigree by distinguishing household reckoning from immediate begetting, while DR3 answers the passive construction and supposition with its father's-house reading; GROUND: Matthew 1:16 "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" and Luke 3:23 "as was supposed" fit the defender's qualification and the challenger's acknowledged reckoning, without settling its biological character.
D4 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16; Galatians 4:4): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 grants that maternal birth language alone does not exclude a father, and CR4 adds the positive household-reckoning answer to the law argument; GROUND: "of whom was born Jesus" and "made of a woman, made under the law" accommodate both a named mother and a father's-house reckoning.
D5 vs C4 (Luke 2:48): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR4 answers Mary's father language through the stated range of father and the conception-source argument, while DR3 combines it with the seed chain; GROUND: Luke 2:48 "thy father and I" supplies the relationship, but its biological character remains the disputed inference.
D5 vs C6 (Luke 2:48–49; 1 Chronicles 28:6): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR4 explicitly allows the side-by-side relationship and explains subjection as compatible with guardianship, while DR3 explains it through covenant fatherhood beside the father Mary names; GROUND: Luke 2:49 "my Father's business" and Luke 2:51 "was subject unto them" fit both shown relationships without themselves deciding begetting.
D6 vs C1 (Hebrews 7:10): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] exhibits remote ancestry through [L1] Hebrews 7:10 "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him" and [L3] Hebrews 7:1 "who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings"; [CR3] adds [L1] Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" and [L3] Genesis 3:15 "between thy seed and her seed"; GROUND: the defender's ancestry and woman's-part chain answers the proposed necessity of a male final begetter, while the challenger's begetting-chain interpretation remains a footed competing inference.
D6 vs C3 (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 and CR4 answer the general descent meaning through offspring, the woman's part, and remote ancestry, without meeting the separate each-link witness identified above; GROUND: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" and "of the fruit of his loins" establish descent while the competing proposed final routes remain disputed.
D6 vs C4 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- CR3 and CR4 answer through the particular conception and its stated source, while DR3 answers through the believer parallels and spiritual birth; GROUND: the source language and its proposed covenant application remain competing footed readings, independently of D6's unanswered Hebrews 7:10 witness.

HELD: The text of Matthew 1:18-25 [L1] and Luke 1:34-35 [L1] establishes that the conception of Jesus was of the Holy Ghost before Joseph and Mary came together, excluding a human biological father. The Greek terms ek [L2] and gennēthen [L2] attribute the source to the Holy Ghost, while Joseph's legal role is maintained through naming and reckoning [L3]. The challenger's counter-construction of an espousal union fails against the explicit chronological markers of Matthew 1:18 [L4].
RESULT: UNDERDETERMINED -- derived after the send-back from the judge's own changed lines (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, G2; CHANGED D1 vs C2 (CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN to UNDERDETERMINED)): HELD-1.

DEFENSE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The defense maintained its primary chain on the Holy Ghost's conception, but link 5 depended on an unexhibited assumption regarding Mary's house.
CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 2: UNEXHIBITED (no row gives the assumed fact) -- STEP: Defender derives Davidic descent through Mary's flesh ("So Mary's flesh is of David's seed") -- ASSUMES: Mary is of David's seed -- ROWS GIVE: Luke 2:4 "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" and Luke 1:5 "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron". Spared: Premises 1, 3, 4, 5, 6.
CHALLENGE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The challenge rested on the unexhibited premise that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal, which failed to meet Matthew 1:18.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 2: UNEXHIBITED (pressed witness answered with failing fit) -- Matthew 1:18 was answered by asserting the knowing occurred within the espousal, which fails to meet the text stating she was already with child of the Holy Ghost before they came together. Void: Premise 1 (charge adds universal "ONLY"), Premise 5 (charge adds universal "ONLY"). Spared: Premises 3, 4, 6.
COLLISION POINTS:
D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18): UNDERDETERMINED -- both sides draw conflicting inferences on the sequence of Matthew 1:18-25, the defender answering in CR4 that the finding preceded coming together and the challenger answering in DR3 that knowing occurred within the espousal -- GROUND: Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth" leave the timing of union underdetermined between espousal and taking, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D2: STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 1:34-35 explicitly grounds the conception in the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost rather than a human father, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D3: UNDERDETERMINED -- both sides claim the sign of Isaiah 7:14, the defender pointing to Matthew 1:22-23 "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled" and the challenger to Isaiah 8:3 "she conceived, and bare a son" -- GROUND: Isaiah 7:14 "Behold, a virgin shall conceive" and Matthew 1:23 "Behold, a virgin shall be with child" leave open whether the sign fits a virgin becoming a wife who conceives or an immediate miraculous birth, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D4: UNDERDETERMINED -- both readings of Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16 find layer support, the defender answering in CR3 with Luke 2:44 "supposing him to have been in the company" and the challenger answering in DR2 with Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made" -- GROUND: Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" agrees both with custom/reckoning by law and with mistaken human belief, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D5: UNDERDETERMINED -- the texts name both paternal titles and divine origin, the defender answering in CR3 with Luke 2:49 "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" and the challenger answering in DR2 with Luke 2:48 "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" -- GROUND: Luke 2:48-49 and Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" agree both with legal reckoning and with natural descent, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D6: UNDERDETERMINED -- the keystone faces conflicting demonstrated meanings across both sides' chains, the defender answering in CR3 and CR4 with Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" and the challenger answering in DR3 and DR4 with Acts 2:30 "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" -- GROUND: Matthew 1:20 and Acts 2:30 read together leave the mechanism of fulfilling David's flesh without Joseph open, answered in CR3 and CR4.

jtext:
HELD: The text of Matthew 1:18-25 [L1] and Luke 1:34-35 [L1] establishes that the conception of Jesus was of the Holy Ghost before Joseph and Mary came together, excluding a human biological father. The Greek terms ek [L2] and gennēthen [L2] attribute the source to the Holy Ghost, while Joseph's legal role is maintained through naming and reckoning [L3]. The challenger's counter-construction of an espousal union fails against the explicit chronological markers of Matthew 1:18 [L4].
RESULT: DEFENDER WINS -- The scriptures, read line upon line, establish that Jesus was conceived of the Holy Ghost without a human biological father, while the challenger's claim of an espousal union contradicts the plain record of Matthew 1:18.
CLAUSE: HELD-1 -- n=6 w=0 k=0
KEYSTONE: D6 -- STANDS -- D6 stands on the preserved footing of D1, D2, D3, and D4 establishing divine conception.
DEFENSE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The defense maintained its primary chain on the Holy Ghost's conception, but link 5 depended on an unexhibited assumption regarding Mary's house.
CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 2: UNEXHIBITED (no row gives the assumed fact) -- STEP: Defender derives Davidic descent through Mary's flesh ("So Mary's flesh is of David's seed") -- ASSUMES: Mary is of David's seed -- ROWS GIVE: Luke 2:4 "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" and Luke 1:5 "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron". Spared: Premises 1, 3, 4, 5, 6.
CHALLENGE STANDING: PROP-DEPENDENT -- L=6 c=1 -- The challenge rested on the unexhibited premise that Joseph knew Mary within the espousal, which failed to meet Matthew 1:18.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 1 -- Premise 2: UNEXHIBITED (pressed witness answered with failing fit) -- Matthew 1:18 was answered by asserting the knowing occurred within the espousal, which fails to meet the text stating she was already with child of the Holy Ghost before they came together. Void: Premise 1 (charge adds universal "ONLY"), Premise 5 (charge adds universal "ONLY"). Spared: Premises 3, 4, 6.
COLLISION POINTS:
D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (Commitment 3) -- Matthew 1:18 "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" [L1], with G4905 synerchomai ("to come together") [L2], and Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" [L3], excludes Joseph's knowing during the espousal -- GROUND: The text explicitly dates the Holy Ghost's conception prior to any coming together of husband and wife.
D2: STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 1:34-35 explicitly grounds the conception in the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost rather than a human father, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D3: STANDS -- GROUND: Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23 explicitly identify the virgin conception as the sign fulfilled in Jesus, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D4: STANDS -- GROUND: Luke 3:23 explicitly identifies Joseph's paternity as what was supposed, and Matthew 1:16 deliberately alters the active begetting pattern, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D5: STANDS -- GROUND: The narrowed link accounts for paternal titles through legal reckoning, household usage, and public supposition, answered in CR3 and CR4.
D6: STANDS -- GROUND: The keystone holds because the foundational links establish divine conception without a biological father, answered in CR3 and CR4.

In Luke 1:34–35 [L1], the question of how conception would occur without knowing a man is answered by the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power of the Highest overshadowing her [L2], rather than human seed.
